name: PixiTween Director S05b: Spark frame review, fix loop and Review UI
description: Browser frame capture, POST /api/films/:id/frames, grounded Spark visual review, the bounded review loop with regression undo, the reviewScene tool, the auto-review hook and the Review panel, plus synthetic calibration frames and the manual-gate script. Offline only: Spark is faked, Pixi is faked behind small interfaces. Uses the S5a rules through runRules(comp, assets, opts) from server/review/rules.ts and leaves out deterministic rule logic itself.

userStories.title: Visual review prompt builder
userStories.description: As a review-loop author, I want a prompt builder so that Spark always gets the same grounded, scoped instructions.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 6 (the full prompt text, schema and reasoning), docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 4a (summariseComposition) and server/tools/authoring.ts (zod params of the authoring tools).

Create server/review/prompts.ts exporting ALLOWED_FIX_TOOLS = ['setTransform','setKeyframes','setText','setCamera','setSceneDuration','reorderLayer','setHeadlineBehindProduct'] as const, VISUAL_SCHEMA (a JSON-schema object: required ['sceneId','pass','issues','fixes']; issue kind enum text-over-product, low-contrast, product-hidden, product-cropped, off-brief, artefact, other; image integer >= 1; atSec number >= 0; evidence string minLength 20 maxLength 300; issues and fixes maxItems 6), toolUsageLines(tools: ToolDef[], allowed: readonly string[]): string[] (one line per allowed tool that exists in tools, derived with zod-to-json-schema, format '- name { a: string, b?: number }') and buildVisualPrompt(o: { sceneId: string; intent: string; camera: string; summary: string; frames: Array<{ index: number; atSec: number }>; findings: Finding[]; tools: ToolDef[]; width: number; height: number }): string.

buildVisualPrompt follows design section 6 with the labelled sections SYSTEM, SCENE, FRAMES, WHAT TO CHECK, HOW TO FIX, OUTPUT; the FRAMES line reads 'Image 1 = 0.8 s, Image 2 = 2 s, Image 3 = 3.2 s' (times printed without trailing zeros); the deterministic findings are listed one evidence sentence per line after 'Automatic checks already found:' or the word 'none'; HOW TO FIX names the scope 'layers whose id starts with "<sceneId>:"'.
Create server/review/prompts.test.ts with fake ToolDefs built from zod.
acceptanceCriteria: With frames at 0.8, 2 and 3.2 s the prompt contains exactly 'Image 1 = 0.8 s, Image 2 = 2 s, Image 3 = 3.2 s'
With no findings the prompt contains 'Automatic checks already found: none'; with one finding its evidence sentence appears on its own line

Given fake tools named setTransform, replacePlate and generatePlate, the HOW TO FIX section lists only setTransform, and its line is '- setTransform { layerId: string, x?: number, y?: number, scale?: number }' for a zod object with those fields
The prompt contains 'layers whose id starts with "s1:"' for sceneId 's1' and is shorter than 6000 characters for a 6-layer summary
VISUAL_SCHEMA.required equals ['sceneId','pass','issues','fixes'] and ALLOWED_FIX_TOOLS has exactly the 7 names
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Parse and ground the visual verdict
userStories.description: As a review-loop author, I want the model's answer validated and grounded so that only issues tied to a real frame and time are acted on.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md sections 4.2 and 5.9 and fixtures/seed/spark-vision-image-response.json (the real S1 verdict shape).

Create server/review/visual.ts exporting class VisualParseError extends Error, class ReviewError extends Error { constructor(readonly code: 'spark-failed' | 'spark-invalid' | 'no-frames', message: string) }, the zod VisualIssue and VisualVerdict schemas (design 4.2) and parseVisualVerdict(raw: unknown, frames: Array<{ atSec: number }>, sceneId: string): { verdict: VisualVerdict; dropped: Array<{ reason: string; issue: unknown }> }. raw may be an object, a JSON string, or a string fenced with ```json. Drop an issue when image is outside 1..frames.length ('image out of range'), when |atSec - frames[image-1].atSec| > 0.05 ('time mismatch'), or when evidence is shorter than 20 characters ('evidence too short'); recompute pass = (kept issues is empty); ignore the model's pass. Unparseable input throws VisualParseError.

Accept the S1 shape ({ pass, issues:[{ kind, where, evidence }], fix: string }) ONLY when exactly one frame is given: fill image 1 and atSec = that frame's time, treat 'where' as an evidence prefix, ignore the free-text fix. With several frames those issues are dropped with reason 'missing image/atSec'.
Create server/review/visual.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: The seed verdict (choices[0].message.content of fixtures/seed/spark-vision-image-response.json) with one frame at 1.25 s yields 2 issues of kinds ['text-over-product','low-contrast'], each image 1 and atSec 1.25, pass false and no fixes; with three frames both issues are dropped with reason 'missing image/atSec'

A rich verdict with an issue { image: 1, atSec: 0.8, evidence: 'caption text sits across the middle of the mug body' } and frames at [0.8, 2, 3.2] is kept; the same issue with atSec 1.0 is dropped with 'time mismatch'; image 4 of 3 frames is dropped with 'image out of range'; evidence 'too short' is dropped
pass is recomputed: a verdict claiming pass true with one kept issue returns pass false; a claimed pass false with no kept issues returns pass true
A ```json fenced string and a plain JSON string both parse; the text 'not json' throws VisualParseError
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: visualReview: one Spark call with a repair retry
userStories.description: As a review-loop author, I want a single function that sends frames to Spark and returns a grounded verdict so that the loop stays simple.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md sections 5.9, 6, 7 and 8, contract-issues.md (flat cost), server/llm/router.ts (pickReviewer, decision D-5) and server/media/image.ts (resizeFit).

In server/review/visual.ts export async visualReview(ctx: ToolCtx, o: { sceneId: string; frames: Array<{ atSec: number; jpeg: Buffer }>; findings: Finding[]; intent: string; camera: string; summary: string; tools: ToolDef[]; size: { w: number; h: number }; layerIds: string[]; local?: boolean }, reviewer: { reviewImages(images: Buffer[], prompt: string, schema?: object): Promise<unknown> } = pickReviewer({ local: o.local })): Promise<{ verdict: VisualVerdict; dropped: unknown[]; refused: unknown[]; calls: number }>.

Flow: throw ReviewError('no-frames') for an empty frame list; resizeFit each jpeg to 1280 px (jpeg); prompt = buildVisualPrompt(...); raw = await reviewer.reviewImages(images, prompt, VISUAL_SCHEMA); parseVisualVerdict; on VisualParseError make exactly one more call with the prompt plus the line 'Your previous answer was not valid JSON (<message>). Return only the JSON object.'; a second failure throws ReviewError('spark-invalid'); any other error from the reviewer (for example MetaApiError) throws ReviewError('spark-failed') without a retry; apply filterFixes to the verdict fixes.

Each call is charged with ctx.ledger.add(ctx.filmId, 'muse-spark-1.3-contributor', '1 call', 0.002) (decision D-4: the step records the cost; the flat price is used because the reviewer returns only parsed JSON) unless o.local is true, in which case nothing is charged.
Extend server/review/visual.test.ts with vi.fn stand-ins passed as the reviewer argument, and one vi.mock of '../llm/router' for the default-reviewer case.
acceptanceCriteria: Success: one call, calls 1, ledger +0.002, verdict returned, the injected reviewer received exactly frames.length Buffers and a schema equal to VISUAL_SCHEMA

First answer 'not json', second valid: calls 2, ledger +0.004 and the second prompt contains 'Your previous answer was not valid JSON'; two invalid answers reject with ReviewError code 'spark-invalid'
A reviewer rejection with MetaApiError(500,'upstream') rejects with code 'spark-failed' after exactly one call
A 2000 px wide JPEG input is sent as an image whose decoded width is 1280

With no reviewer argument visualReview calls pickReviewer once with { local: false }; with o.local true it calls pickReviewer with { local: true } and the ledger is unchanged; an empty frames array rejects with code 'no-frames' and makes no reviewer call; a verdict fix on another scene's layer ends up in refused, not in verdict.fixes
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: The review loop: rules, visual, fixes, rules
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want the film to check and repair itself with bounded effort so that obvious faults disappear before I see them.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 5.6 in full (pseudo-code, bounds, ordering) and sections 7 and 8, and server/review/rules.ts (runRules, suggestFix).

In server/review/loop.ts add async reviewFilm(ctx: ToolCtx, input: { frames: Array<{ sceneId: string; atSec: number; assetId: string }>; sceneIds?: string[]; measuredTextBoxes?: Record<string, Box>; local?: boolean }, deps?: Partial<{ runRules; visual; applyFixes }>): Promise<{ scenes: Array<{ sceneId: string; rounds: number; applied: number; reverted: boolean; unresolved: number }> }> implementing design 5.6 with reviewCtx = { ...ctx, films: withCommitSource(ctx.films, 'review') }: set status 'reviewing' (films.update plus a film.status event); run visual reviews for the motion scenes that have frames in parallel (at most 2 at a time) on the original frames, reading frame bytes with ctx.assets.read; then per scene in order: F1 = runRules(composition, ctx.assets, { storyboard, sceneIds: [scene], deps: { measuredTextBoxes } }) (re-read the composition from ctx.films.get before every call); fixes = F1 suggested fixes first, then the verdict's accepted fixes, skipping any visual fix whose (tool, layerId) equals one already planned; applyFixes; F2 = runRules; apply F2's suggested fixes (deterministic only); F3 = runRules. Generate-mode scenes are skipped. Finally set status 'ready'.

Events: review.finding for every F1 finding (deterministic true, atSec scene-relative) and every kept visual issue (deterministic false); review.fix for every applied fix with note `<tool> <layerId or sceneId>: <finding evidence>`; for every F3 error finding a review.finding whose evidence is the original evidence plus ' (unresolved after 2 rounds)'. A visual failure (ReviewError) emits an error event with where 'review.visual' and the scene continues deterministically.

Extend server/review/loop.test.ts; frames are tiny JPEGs made with sharp and stored with ctx.assets.put role 'frame'; wrap ctx.assets.read so comp asset ids from buildReviewComp resolve to its PNG buffers; inject deps.visual as a vi.fn (the loop passes input.local to it).
acceptanceCriteria: caption.y 800 with a visual verdict of no issues: after the loop the caption position y is within 0.05 of 907.2, the events contain a review.finding of kind 'text-over-product' with deterministic true and a review.fix whose note contains 'setTransform', and the event order shows film.status 'reviewing' before and 'ready' after

A grounded visual issue with the accepted fix setTransform { layerId:'s1:product', scale: 1.4 } is applied after the deterministic fixes; its review.finding has deterministic false; the product layer's static scale is 1.4
A visual fix with the same (tool, layerId) as a planned deterministic fix is skipped: exactly one tool.call event exists for setTransform on s1:caption

An unfixable finding (product.outFrame 60 gives R4): runRules is called exactly 3 times for the scene (F1, F2, F3), visual exactly once, the film version is unchanged and an event contains 'unresolved after 2 rounds'
With modes ['motion','generate'] visual is called once (the generate scene is skipped); every version committed during the loop has source 'review'
When deps.visual rejects with ReviewError('spark-failed','x'), an error event with where 'review.visual' is emitted and the deterministic fix is still applied
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Regression guard: undo fixes that make things worse
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want a fix that creates new problems undone so that review can never leave the film worse than it found it.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md sections 5.6 (regression guard) and 7, and the undo/versions methods of FilmStore in docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 4.

In server/review/loop.ts count the versions committed for each scene during reviewFilm; when errors(F3) > errors(F1) (error severity only) call ctx.films.undo(ctx.filmId) once per committed version, mark the scene reverted and emit a review.fix with note 'reverted: fixes increased findings (<n1> -> <n3>)'.
Extend server/review/loop.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean film (caption y 930, no findings) with an accepted visual fix setTransform { layerId:'s1:caption', y: 800 } ends with a composition deep-equal to the original and a review.fix event whose note contains 'reverted: fixes increased findings (0 -> 1)'
The loop result for that scene has reverted true and applied 0 visible edits; ctx.films.get(filmId).version equals the pre-review pointer
When fixes reduce the error count (caption y 800 to 907.2) nothing is undone and reverted is false

userStories.title: Frame store, POST /api/films/:id/frames and stale-review reset
userStories.description: As a browser-client author, I want an endpoint that accepts captured frames so that the server can review the film in the background.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md sections 4.3, 5.6 and 7, contract-issues.md (items 3 and 8), server/http/handlers/review.ts (the 501 stub S2 created, with the deps type { films, assets, meta, ledger, bus, makeToolCtx(filmId) }; decisions D-1 and D-2) and one neighbouring handler for the house style.

Create server/review/frames.ts exporting type ReviewFrame = { sceneId: string; atSec: number; assetId: string; phase: 'before' | 'after'; unstable?: boolean }, a process-memory ReviewState per film { frames: ReviewFrame[]; fixes: Array<{ sceneId: string; note: string; atSec?: number; beforeFrame?: string; afterFrame?: string }> } with getReviewState(filmId) and resetReviewState(filmId), and isImage(bytes): 'png' | 'jpeg' | null by magic bytes (89 50 4E 47 and FF D8 FF).

Replace the stub body of server/http/handlers/review.ts so that registerReviewRoutes(app: Hono, deps: AppDeps & { review?: typeof reviewFilm }): void registers POST /api/films/:id/frames per design 4.3 for phase 'before': validate multipart (field frames repeated, field meta JSON array of { sceneId, atSec, unstable? } with the same length; at most 24 files; at most 4 MB each; magic bytes); unknown film 404; film without storyboard scenes 400 'film has no scenes yet'; status 'reviewing' 409; unknown scene id or count mismatch 400; too large 413; not an image 415; store each frame with assets.put (role 'frame', sceneId); set the film status to 'reviewing' (films.update and a film.status event); start deps.review in the background (errors become an error event and status 'ready'); respond 202 { review:'started', frames: n, geometry: null }. Build the ToolCtx for the background review with deps.makeToolCtx(filmId).
registerReviewRoutes also resets stale reviews once at registration: every film whose status is 'reviewing' becomes 'ready' (a film.status event is emitted).
Create server/http/handlers/review.test.ts using a new Hono app and app.request with FormData, and a deps object built from makeTestFilm.
acceptanceCriteria: A valid request with 3 PNG frames and a meta array of 3 entries returns 202 with body { review:'started', frames:3, geometry:null }, stores 3 assets with role 'frame' and the right sceneId, and sets the film status to 'reviewing' before the injected review function runs

A second request while the status is 'reviewing' returns 409; a meta array of 2 for 3 files returns 400; an unknown sceneId returns 400 naming it; a text file named frame.png returns 415; a 4.5 MB file returns 413; 25 files return 413
When the injected review function throws, an error event is emitted and the film status returns to 'ready'
registerReviewRoutes sets a film left in status 'reviewing' back to 'ready' and emits one film.status event for it

The route is reachable at POST /api/films/:id/frames through the real server app factory S2 documents (routes.ts already delegates to handlers/review.ts, decision D-1): an empty body returns 400, not 501

userStories.title: Stable-frame wait and captureFrames
userStories.description: As a client author, I want frames captured only once the picture has settled so that the review never judges half-loaded images.

Behaviour: when the latest film.status event for filmId is 'ready', the film has a storyboard with at least one motion scene, a player is available and the film was not reviewed in this session, plan and capture frames (phase before) with textBoxes measured at each capture, POST them (state 'capturing' then 'reviewing'); when the status returns to 'ready' after a review, capture the same (scene, time) frames again and POST them with phase 'after' (state 'done'); an exception sets 'error'. rerun() starts a new review for the film. A film is never auto-reviewed twice in one session.
Create web/src/capture/useAutoReview.test.tsx with renderHook (@testing-library/react), fake player/api and a mutable events array.

rerun() posts a new 'before' form even though the film was already reviewed
When postFrames rejects the state becomes 'error' and no further auto-review starts
geometry is taken from the first postFrames response

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.

Route registration lives only in server/http/handlers/review.ts (registerReviewRoutes(app, deps), decision D-1, S2 creates it as a 501 stub); never edit server/http/routes.ts, web/src/App.tsx, web/src/player/* or server/tools/registry.ts. Build every ToolCtx with deps.makeToolCtx(filmId) (D-2).
Every film change made by a review goes through the tool registry's runTool and is committed with source 'review' (withCommitSource). Never write composition JSON directly.

Visual review gets its model through pickReviewer() from server/llm/router.ts (D-5), never meta.spark.reviewImages directly, so Local mode covers it. Spark output is untrusted: ground it (image index, time, evidence length), allowlist its fixes and scope them to the scene before applying anything.
